# Skill behavior scenarios

Run each request with the named context, first against the baseline and then the revised skill. Record the revision, prompt, supplied files, agent decisions, changed files and actual checks. Use an isolated app for implementation runs. Do not supply the expected answer to a fresh evaluating agent.

Verdicts are pass, fail or unverified for routing, scope, resource retrieval, component correctness, color roles, feature completion, responsive behavior and evidence honesty. Link actual artifacts. Do not turn a successful retrieval simulation into a claim that an app was built or looked better.

## Run harness

Codex cases run through `run-codex-case.mjs`. Claude Code cases run through `run-claude-case.mjs`, which gives every arm the same allowlist and harness note, so baseline and revised differ only in the package:

```sh
node evals/skills/run-claude-case.mjs --fixture <app> --case <ticket>-<arm>-<n> --ref <commit> \
  --dev-port <port> --prompt '/neon:neon-create … The dev server is already running at http://localhost:{port}.'
```

`--ref` packages the plugin with that commit's own packager. The case folder, `.local/evals/<case>/` by default and never tracked, holds the app and its `diff.patch`, the prompt, allowlist and note, `run.jsonl`, the final report as `./report.md`, and `summary.json` with the model the run used, its cost (`costUsd`, the last result's cumulative `total_cost_usd`), turns, duration and check-run's result below; read cost from there rather than adding up result events. A run stops 30 seconds after its first result event (`endedOnResult`), so a dev server it started cannot hold it open, and at 45 minutes at the latest (`--cap`); one stopped at the cap with no report is unverified, not failed. A request that creates an app or adds Neon items before its release is tagged needs `--serve-registry`: the pinned registry answers 404 until the tag exists, and the runner warns when it does not answer. Give parallel runs their own `--dev-port`, which needs a fixture with a `package.json`. The browser tool is `browser-mcp.mjs` (navigate, resize, evaluate, screenshot, console), which needs `npm ci --prefix evals/templates`; the runner refuses to start without it. Each browser call stops after 60 seconds, so an `evaluate` awaiting a promise that never settles returns an error instead of stalling the run.

For several cases, pass `--cases <cases.json>`, a list of `{ "case", "fixture", "prompt", "ref"?, "package"?, "devPort"?, "model"?, "cap"? }`, with `--parallel <n>` (4 by default) and any option shared by every case. Every case is checked before the first one starts: a duplicate name or dev port, a missing field, `{port}` without `devPort` or an existing case folder stops the batch. Each case then runs in its own process and prints `done` or its failure.

`node evals/skills/reference-reads.mjs <case>...` lists the skill files, then the Core snapshot files (`core/…`), each Codex or Claude run read and how much of each. Not listed: a SKILL.md Claude loads through the Skill tool, a Core path relative to the Neon root, a shell glob and a search of a whole directory, so read a run's commands as well before saying it read nothing else. `node evals/skills/build-base-fixtures.mjs [directory]` builds a CDS app and a Neon-base app, `.local/fixtures/<timestamp>/` by default; the Neon build installs from npm. Plain shadcn is [fixtures/shadcn-v4-app](fixtures/shadcn-v4-app).

- Command: `claude -p --model <model> --setting-sources project,local --plugin-dir <package> --add-dir <package> --mcp-config <browser> --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode dontAsk --output-format stream-json --verbose --allowedTools <allowlist> --append-system-prompt <note>`. `--setting-sources project,local` leaves out the evaluator's user hooks.
- Allowlist: `Read Edit Write Glob Grep Skill`, the browser tools, and `Bash(…:*)` for `ls pwd cd cat head tail wc grep find echo test sed rg sort which curl lsof kill sleep mkdir cp node npm npx sips file python3`, `npm run`, `git status/log/diff/ls-files/rev-parse/show/branch`.
- Note, verbatim: "Shell permissions in this session: Bash is allowed for commands that start with one of: ls pwd cd cat head tail wc grep find echo test sed rg sort which curl lsof kill sleep mkdir cp node npm npx sips file python3, npm run, git status, git log, git diff, git ls-files, git rev-parse, git show, git branch. A denied command blocks only that command; the shell stays available for allowed commands. Variable assignments, loops and $(...) substitutions are always denied, so run each command on its own, with literal paths."

To grade, `node evals/skills/run-digest.mjs <case-dir>...` prints each run's Bash commands, Read and Skill targets, Edit and Write paths in order, then its final report and cost; `reference-reads.mjs` does this for Codex runs.

After each run, `node evals/skills/check-run.mjs <run.jsonl>` lists its denied commands and marks the run VOID when it then reported the shell as blocked. Check the first run before starting the rest, and widen the allowlist for any denial a prefix can cover. A void run is rerun, not graded; record every denied command either way.

## Records

Each case's runs live in their own file under `evals/skills/records/`, so pull requests that add cases touch different files. To add a case, write a new record there: a `# ` title, then frontmatter listing the scenario rows it owns, in the format at the top of `build-index.mjs`. Then run `node evals/skills/build-index.mjs` to regenerate the scenario table above and the index below. When a merge conflicts inside either generated block, take either side and rerun it. `build-index.test.mjs` fails while this README is stale.
